system.summary: Monoalphabetic substitution in graphic signs with a few homophones (a, e, n, o, r, t, u), word divisions kept, clear words mixed in, and some code groups.
system.doubled_letters: special sign for ss, verified in known-plaintext facesse and imparasse; other doubles not fully inventoried
system.sibling_key: 1479-80 Sadoleto-Naples key (ASMo Cifrario b. 4 fasc. 1) not digitised, not used
system.notes: Key in key_working.md uses its own H/M/L confidence scale. Follow-up verified literal alphabetic dom, and X's Venetian-government referent from R1106/26b; exact lexical expansion unspecified. Total unread groups unknown because the facing-page cipher is not fully transcribed. See verified_groups.md.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary clear copies of R1101 (7a) and R1106 (26a/26b) and decipherments of R1104 (13a/13b) on Vestigia; none for R1102 or R1103

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: 2026-09-20: Python standard library and Pillow; web search; visual image inspection

solution.what: Vestigia, MDE, Cremonini and Tomokiyo checked; letters never printed.
DECODE metadata and images for R1100-R1118 fetched with the cookie; Vestigia search found clear copies 7a, 13a/13b, 26a/26b.
Key built by aligning R1101 with 7a and R1104 with 13a.
R1102 cipher block read in gist: the Venetian offer of Veglia, the fleet command for Matthias's son and 100,000 a year.
R1103 faded block yields fragments only.

Reopened original R1102 I5657 spread: the seven-line bottom-left cipher block is followed by substantial cipher on the right page. Prior seven-line-only description is incomplete. Reassessing unresolved glyphs and the continuation.

Reopened Matyus in Vestigia III pp. 150 and 160-163. The separate 20 June letter explicitly names Don Francesco, Ferrante's son. Fresh targeted searches found no independent decipherment of R1102/R1103; project search results were excluded as corroboration.

R1102 facing-page opening ducati confirms currency. Additional extracts read include the closing secrecy clause and, in a separate later passage, ducati ogni anno sino a sei o septe anni. Recruitment wording remains tentative; see coordinate-referenced review.

Informant title may read alphabetically dom: compare its d with adjacent da, comma-shaped o with como, and final 4 with m. Francesco d'Aragona is a contextual candidate, not an established decipherment. R1101 control inspection did not resolve X; connective-word guesses were not accepted.

Downloaded public Vestigia replies 1252, 1250, 1251 using fetch_replies.py after sandbox network access failed and an escalated retry succeeded. Inspected their written pages and versos; October reply discusses 100,000 annually, September reply names Don Francesco, but no direct expansion of X was established.
Surveyed cached Vestigia 1294 photographs and re-examined enhanced R1103 strips. No additional continuous plaintext accepted; repeated photographs are not independent clear-text witnesses.

Matched each sign of R1102's title to adjacent da, como and milia, establishing literal alphabetic dom. Historical identification as Francesco d'Aragona remains an inference. Coordinates and comparison image recorded in verified_groups.md.

Located the repeated X group in R1106 manuscript p. 3 l. 3, after in guera a. Aligned with contemporary clear witness 26b/Vestigia 4004 l. 2 naming the Signoria di Venetia. Venetian-government referent now verified; surrounding wording differs, so a unique lexical expansion is not claimed.

Re-examined unboxed R1102 strips: fi-/gliolo, per loro capitaneo, and de l'armata replace prior figlio, loco and uncertain arma. The parenthesis around e bastardo is actually present. Connective phrase in ll. 3-4 remains unread.

Full-page survey of R1102 pp. 1 and 4 found a further cipher line on p. 4. Faint ordinary writing above parts may be a partial interlinear decipherment; extent unverified. Added cipher_inventory.md so subsequent coverage includes pp. 2-4 and separates image numbers from manuscript pages.

Inspected R1102 p. 4 with wider clear context: faint ordinary annotations align directly above the cipher, but opening and final groups remain unresolved. Split the short p. 3 cipher crop and read gli poteriano fare [...] / grande partito che [...] non [...]. Recorded only these extracts, source coordinates and uncertainty in reading_r1102_additional.md.

Surveyed outer pages 152/155; no sign-cipher found there. Opening, middle and ending anchors connect 26b to page 3 through the final mixed paragraph. No unmatched principal region found, but internal word-level coverage remains unverified, so plaintext.partial stays unknown. Added alignment_r1106.md and contrast view of full 26b.

Whole-letter witness is supported at boundaries, but internal omissions remain untested; changed plaintext.partial from false to unknown and documented alignment_r1101.md.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was built by aligning R1101 with its contemporary clear copy 7a and R1104 with its decipherment 13a, both in the same ASMo Ambasciatori Ungheria b. 1/9 file (found on Vestigia), then applied to R1102 and R1103, which have no clear copy.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Not measurable: no token-marked reading of the whole group; R1102 working edition keeps 20 unresolved U labels over partial page-3/4 transcriptions (cipher_inventory.md: 'not a symbol count'), R1103 has no transcription, R1101/R1106 read via contemporary clear witnesses not collated word by word. Value from NOTES
outcome.notes: Research reopened and in progress. R1101/R1106 have contemporary clear witnesses; R1102 coverage expanded to facing p. 3. Literal dom and X's Venetian-government referent verified. Several passages remain unread; R1103 still yields fragments. No end-to-end solution or publication in the 20 Sep session. fraction_read 0.65 is an estimate from the notes: R1101 and R1106 covered by contemporary clear copies, R1102 read in gist with unresolved labels, R1103 fragments only; not a token count. fraction_read 0.65 is an estimate from the notes: R1101 and R1106 covered by contemporary clear copies, R1102 read in gist with unresolved labels, R1103 fragments only; not a token count.
